q: 1. An advantage of plane tabling is ...............
options: changes to miss details are less
explain: Because plotting happens in the field while looking at the terrain, the surveyor is less likely to omit important details.

q: 2. The instrument which is used in plane tabling for obtaining horizontal and vertical distances directly without resorting to chaining, is known as
explain: A telescopic alidade fitted with stadia hairs allows horizontal and vertical distances to be read directly (by tacheometric principles) without chaining, unlike a plain alidade which is only a sighting/ruling device.

q: 3. Plotting of inaccessible points on a plane table, is done by
explain: Inaccessible points (points that cannot be reached to measure distance) are plotted by the method of intersection, sighting the point from two known plane table stations and drawing rays to fix its position.

q: 4. Methods adopted for traversing are
options: chain traversing and loose needle method
chain angle method and fast needle method
explain: Traversing can be done using various methods such as 'loose needle' (compass), 'fast needle' (theodolite), or by measuring angles between lines using a chain.

q: 5. Radiation plane table survey is the best suited when
explain: Radiation requires measuring the actual distance from the instrument station to each point, so it is best suited when the points are both close by and physically accessible for chaining.

q: 6. The 'fix' of a plane table station with three known points, is bad if the plane station lies
options: on the circumference of the circumscribing circle
explain: If the station lies on the circle passing through the three control points (the great circle), the position is indeterminate because all points on that arc will satisfy the angular conditions.

q: 7. Accuracy of 'fix' by two point problem, is
explain: The two-point problem is generally considered less accurate and less reliable than the three-point problem due to the lack of a third check-line to confirm the position.

q: 8. The process of putting the plane table into some fixed position so that a line representing certain direction of the plane is parallel to the direction in the field is known as
explain: Orientation is the process of aligning the plane table so that lines drawn on the sheet are parallel to the corresponding lines/directions on the ground.

q: 9. Accurate centering of a plane table is done by
explain: A plumbing fork (with a plumb bob) is the instrument used to accurately centre the plane table exactly over the ground station point.

q: 10. The working edge of an alidade, is known as
explain: The straight ruling edge of an alidade against which sighting/drawing lines are drawn is specifically called the fiducial edge.

q: 11. In the method of plane table survey the object to be plotted is sighted from two plane table stations. This method is called as
explain: Sighting the same object from two different, known plane table stations and plotting its position at the intersection of the two resulting rays is the method of intersection.

q: 12. Finding the location of the station occupied by the table, on the sheet by means of sighting to three well defined points whose locations have been previously plotted on the sheet, is known as
explain: This specific technique of locating the occupied plane table station using three known, already-plotted points is called the three-point problem.

q: 13. In Indian tangent clinometer is associated with .............
explain: The Indian tangent clinometer is used primarily in Plane Table surveying to determine the elevations of points by measuring vertical angles.

q: 14. The instrument used for accurate centering in plane table survey is .............
explain: A plumbing fork (U-frame) with a plumb bob is used to center the point on the paper exactly over the station on the ground.

q: 15. The method of surveying in which field work and plotting work are done simultaneously, is called
explain: As established, plane table surveying is the unique method where field observation and plotting proceed together, simultaneously.

q: 16. In plane tabling, the instrument used to measure horizontal and vertical distances directly, is known as
explain: As noted earlier, a telescopic alidade, fitted with stadia hairs, allows both horizontal and vertical distances to be measured directly in plane table surveying.

q: 17. The operation of turning the table so that all the lines on the paper are parallel to the corresponding lines on the ground, is called
explain: As defined earlier, this act of aligning the plane table so that plotted lines are parallel to the corresponding ground lines is called orientation.

q: 18. The method of intersection in plane tabling is commonly used for
options: locating the distant and inaccessible points
locating the points which may be used subsequently as the instrument stations
explain: Intersection is a versatile method used to locate distant/inaccessible points, broken boundary details, and even future instrument stations, so all the listed uses apply.

q: 19. Spirit level in plane table is used for
explain: The spirit level fitted to (or used with) a plane table is specifically used to check and set the table perfectly horizontal, i.e., for levelling the table.

q: 20. The types of survey in which field work and plotting proceeds simultaneously
explain: Plane table surveying is unique because the map is drawn in the field while the observations are being made.

q: 21. Plane table surveying is graphical method of surveying in which
options: field work and plotting proceeds simultaneously
plotting is done later while records are taken in field book
explain: The primary advantage of plane table surveying is that the map is prepared in the field directly, eliminating the need for a separate field book.

q: 22. Locating the position of plane table station with reference to three known points, is known as .............
explain: The three-point problem is a resection technique used to find the location of the instrument station by sighting three known mapped points.

q: 23. A disadvantage of plane table survey is
options: It is heavy, cumbersome and awkward to carry
It can't be used in wet climate
details may not be available while redrawing to a different scale
accessories are likely to be lost
explain: The large board and tripod make it physically more difficult to transport compared to a compass or a simple level.

q: 24. Orientation is the operation of keeping the table at successive stations such that
options: the position of the table at the station is parallel to the position it occupied at the previous station
the position of station plotted on sheet is exactly above the corresponding station on ground
the table is brought in a horizontal plane
explain: Orientation ensures that every line on the paper remains parallel to its corresponding line on the ground.

q: 25. The method of plane tabling generally adopted to obtain details and plotting inaccessible points is
explain: Intersection plots points by the crossing of rays from two different stations, which is ideal for points that cannot be reached to measure distance.

q: 26. In the intersection method of plane tabling the number of stations needed to be set up are
explain: At least two known stations are required to create the intersecting rays for a single point.

q: 27. Resection is the method employed for
explain: Resection is specifically used to establish the location of the plane table on the map by observing known points.

q: 28. The size of plane table is
explain: A standard plane table used in surveying is typically about 600 mm x 750 mm in size, as given by this text.

q: 29. The two- point problem as compared to the three point problem is
explain: The two-point problem involves more steps and temporary setups compared to the three-point problem.

q: 30. The three point problem can be solved by
explain: Several methods exist to solve the three-point problem, including Lehmann's (trial and error) and Bessel's (graphical).

q: 31. The size of plane table is
explain: Standard surveying plane tables typically measure 600mm by 750mm.

q: 32. The process of aligning the plane table by rotating it in the horizontal plane to the corresponding lines on the ground
explain: Rotation to align with ground features is the definition of orientation.

q: 33. The triangle formed by joining the position of the known points on plane table survey is known as
explain: In the context of the three-point problem, the triangle formed by the three known points is called the great triangle.

q: 34. In case of resection method of plane table, the relation between great triangle and great circle are
options: the area of great triangle is more than great circle
the area of great triangle is less than great circle
the area of great triangle is equal to great circle
explain: Geometrically, the circle passing through the three points (great circle) encloses the triangle (great triangle).

q: 35. Three-point problem can be solved by
explain: The three-point problem for orienting a plane table can be solved by several standard techniques, including the tracing paper method, Bessel's (mechanical/graphical) method, and Lehmann's method, so all are valid solutions.

q: 36. A poor fix of the table is
options: when station is within the great triangle
when station is near the great circle
explain: If the instrument station lies on or near the circle passing through the three known points, the solution becomes unreliable.

q: 37. The strength of fix' is poor when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the station is outside the great circle
the station is on the great circle
the station is within the great circle but outside the great triangle
explain: The position is indeterminate if the station is on the circumference of the great circle. [2] the station is within the great circle but outside the great triangle become the 2nd bestnchoice

q: 38. The two point problem and three point problems are methods of
explain: Both problems solve for the station's location and the table's orientation simultaneously.

q: 39. To orient a plane table without two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted is
explain: The two-point problem is the specific procedure used to orient when only two points are available and distance measurement is not possible.

q: 40. Which one of the following is not a personal error ?
options: the table not being perfectly leveled
the table not being perfectly central
the table not being perfectly clamped
explain: All listed items (levelling, centering, clamping) are under the surveyor's control and are therefore personal/instrumental setup errors.

q: 41. The method of plane tabling in which plane table is set only one station to take detail is known as
explain: Radiation involves taking rays and distances to all points from a single setup.

q: 42. Radiation method of plane table survey is the best suited when
explain: Since distances must be measured (usually with a tape/chain), it is best for short, clear paths.

q: 43. In plane table instrument for horizontal & vertical measurement without chaining
explain: A telescopic alidade is equipped with stadia hairs for distance and a vertical circle for slope angles.

q: 44. Which instrument is not used in plane table ?
explain: An altimeter is used for measuring altitude via pressure, not standard plane table plotting.

q: 45. The size of plane table is .............
explain: While various sizes exist, the standard size for a large plane table used in professional surveying is typically 600 mm x 750 mm.

q: 46. The technique of plotting all the accessible stations with a single set up of plane table is called
explain: As stated in Q104, this technique of plotting all accessible points from a single plane table setup is called radiation.

q: 47. In case of telescopic alidade, the adjustment done is
options: the line of collimation should perpendicular to the axis of telescope
the horizontal axis should be parallel to the alidade rule
the bubble line of telescope level should be parallel to the plane of collimation
explain: Telescopic alidades require these permanent adjustments to ensure the line of sight accurately reflects the horizontal and vertical positions plotted on the sheet.

q: 48. An instrument resembling an alidade is
explain: A tangent clinometer (or Indian clinometer) consists of two vanes similar to an alidade and is used on a plane table to determine the heights of objects.

q: 49. Usefulness of plane table is enhanced by providing
explain: The Indian tangent clinometer allows the plane table surveyor to determine the heights of points and ground slopes effectively.

q: 50. A point determined by resection on a plane table is called
explain: A 'fix' is the location of the plane table instrument station on the drawing sheet determined through the resection process.

q: 51. The instrument which is used in plane tabling for obtaining horizontal and vertical distance directly without resorting to chaining, is known as
explain: A telescopic alidade is equipped with stadia hairs, allowing the surveyor to compute distances and elevations optically rather than using a tape or chain.

q: 52. The type of surveying which requires least office work is
explain: Since the map is drawn directly in the field, plane table surveying eliminates the need for extensive office calculations and plotting.

q: 53. Intersection method of detailed plotting is most suitable for
explain: Intersection is ideal for hilly or broken ground where measuring distances with a chain or tape is difficult or impossible.

q: 54. The operation of turning the table so all lines are parallel to corresponding ground lines is
explain: Orientation is the process of keeping the table at each successive station parallel to its position at the first station.

q: 55. The plotting of small areas commanded from a single station is usually done by
explain: Radiation is the simplest method where points are plotted by drawing rays from a single instrument station and measuring distances along those rays.

q: 56. The method of intersection in plane tabling is commonly used for
explain: Intersection allows the surveyor to plot points (like a church spire or a peak) that cannot be reached or chained easily.

q: 57. The method of plane tabling commonly used for establishing instrument stations only is
explain: Resection is primarily used to determine the location of the instrument station itself on the map using previously plotted points.

q: 58. The method of surveying in which field work and plotting work are done simultaneously, is called .............
explain: Plane table surveying is unique because the map is drawn in the field while observations are being made.

q: 59. In plate tabling, the instrument used to measure horizontal and vertical distance directly is known as .............
explain: A telescopic alidade is equipped with a telescope and stadia hairs, allowing the surveyor to determine distances and elevations without manual chaining.
